text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key idea is using good naming conventions. Choose clear, meaningful names for variables and functions so others can quickly see what they do. Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes the code simpler to test and change. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because fixing bugs or adding new features takes less time. In short, writing readable code helps your whole team work faster and with fewer mistakes.
